analysis: The PR makes official CI-built signed provider releases auto-register with the coordinator through the existing release API (publish-release job, RELEASE_KEY, provider-release-publication.py publish at line 1119). It drops per-release hardware qualification and manual approval, and drops environment approvals on release jobs (workflow comment lines 22-25). provider-trust.md item 4 (head, ~line 79) now says CI and repository writers are trusted for build identity. This contradicts the canonical statements in A-017, T-054 and the header (operator-approved qualification; CI release keys cannot grant approval). The threat model needs updating. A secret-holding compromise of CI, or of the release key, now yields serving authorization for App Attest providers without an independent approval. Signing and notarization, immutable artifact retention, resume verification (verify-source from master) and the source-sha binding are preserved. I could not see the actual scripts (provider-release-publication.py, provider-release-resume.py, coordinator release handlers and persistence), so how qualification rows are created, scoped or revoked in the coordinator remains unreviewed. Next pass: check that revocation tombstones still block re-registration, that the release API is scoped to this registration, and that tag and ancestry verification is enforced. The workflow file is shown in full but not as a diff, so some changes may be pre-existing.

findings.detail: The publish-release job registers the exact signed build with the coordinator using the env-scoped RELEASE_KEY, and the changelog and provider-trust.md state that per-release hardware qualification and manual approval are no longer required. The canonical model (A-017, T-054, TB-011 and the header notes) says an independently authenticated operator approves the exact binary and CodeDirectory, and that CI release keys cannot grant approval. A leaked PROD_RELEASE_KEY, or any repository writer who can run the workflow, can now register an arbitrary signed build. A build that passes only Apple signing then qualifies for protocol-3 serving. The remaining runtime checks (Apple proof, receipt, revocation) do not verify what the build does with plaintext prompts. Release jobs also no longer require environment approval (workflow header comment, lines 22-25). Fix: update A-005, A-017, T-054, T-024 and TB-011 to name CI and repository-writer compromise as an explicit trust dependency. Consider a re-introduced approval gate or protected environment for prod, a release key scoped to registration only, and alerting or a delay on new qualified hashes.
findings.title: CI release key now confers App Attest build qualification; threat model still says it cannot

findings.detail: In the publish-release job, the 'Install publication tools' step runs pip install awscli with no version or hash pinning, then prepends the venv bin directory to GITHUB_PATH. The next step runs provider-release-publication.py publish with RELEASE_KEY and the R2 credentials in its environment. A compromised awscli or transitive dependency, or a hijacked PyPI release, could read the production release key and R2 credentials. Because registration now implies serving qualification, this supply-chain path matters more than before. Fix: pin awscli with hashes, or use a vendored or preinstalled runner tool, and keep third-party tooling out of the process that carries the release key.
findings.title: Unpinned awscli installed from PyPI into the job that holds the release key
